- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5-7 days); apply downward bias to first 5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 10-15% if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price is trending down; use sentiment as a “confidence filter” — if sentiment > 0.67 but price drops, reduce forecast by 5-10%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3-5 days of history show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 65-70 range), model tends to ignore it; apply a “mean reversion buffer” to cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day average.
